title.narrative: Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation Corridors 1 and 6 Connector Road (Aktobe-Kandyagash) Reconstruction Project

description.narrative:
The proposed project will (i) reconstruct the 89-kilometer highway connecting Aktobe and Kandyagash, and (ii) strengthen the institutional capacity of KazAvtoZhol.
The project is aligned with the following impact: more jobs created, and Kazakhstan integrated into the regional and global economic system. The project will have the following outcome: efficient, reliable, and safe movement of people and goods in West Kazakhstan increased. Output 1: Aktobe-Kandyagash highway reconstructed to category I standard. The project will upgrade the 89-km two-lane category II and III road to a four-lane category I road that will connect Aktobe to Kandyagash. The project will widen the road to the category I standard with climate-resilient features, construct roadside service areas with sanitary facilities especially for women, reconstruct all bridges, build two new bypasses of villages, and improve road safety.
Output 2: Institutional capacity of KazAvtoZhol strengthened. This output will strengthen KazAvtoZhol's institutional capacity by providing equipment; staffing; and training on financial management, procurement, project management, gender, and social safeguards management. The training sessions will include a minimum of 30% participation by women.

Output: Institutional capacity of KazAvtoZhol strengthened Indicator: At least 100 KazAvtoZhol staff (50% of whom are women) applied their increased knowledge and skills on project management Achievement: N Progress/Status: As confirmed, KAZH conducts various capacity-building training courses for its employees using own funds as part of company's efforts to improve and upgrade their qualifications. The topics of such training are compiled and earmarked on annual basis. The lists of training sessions completed in 2023- 2024 focused on financial management, practical application of FIDIC contracts terms, critical thinking, etc. As part of project contribution, the CSC provided online training for KAZH headquarters and Branch office staff on 11-14 November 2024 on contract management and procurement. The training proceedings including the agenda, participants' name, presentation slides, and the feedback received from the participants have been provided to ADB. Overall, 104 staff were trained in 2023-2025, of whom 50 (48%) were women and 54 (52%) were men. If post training survey on application of learning from project management has not yet been conducted, KAZH will (i) conduct such survey among the trained staff (including the women) on trainings to inquire about the relevance, usefulness of trainings, and application of the concepts /knowledge, tools in their work and (ii) provide a brief report with survey results. Data Source: Participants' feedback survey conducted by KazAvtozhol. Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2024 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: Institutional capacity of KazAvtoZhol strengthened Indicator: Environment and social safeguards unit (with 30% female staff) established Achievement: N Progress/Status: The Department of Technical Policy and Control (DTPC) in KAZH is responsible for reviewing and approval of safeguards documents at project preparation and approval stages. In 2024, a new Department of External Loans (DELs) was established in KAZH to oversee IFI-financed loans, including the safeguards monitoring responsibilities. Since then, a sole staff in DELs had been overseeing both environmental and social safeguards and dealing with local governments on safeguard related matters until May 2025. Considering the growing number of IFI-and-government funded projects and the importance of mitigating potential impacts to environment and social condition, KAZH merged two departments and established a new Department of Project Implementation (DPI) in May 2025. The DPI is responsible for safeguards among others, reports to Deputy Chairman of KAZH, and currently has one safeguard staff responsible for both environment and social safeguards. Further, KAZH is considering potential enhancement of functional capacity of the DPI and will consider recruiting the dedicated staff separately for environmental and social safeguards. The Mission highlighted that at least one additional safeguards specialist should be engaged within the DPI to ensure effective and smooth implementation of safeguards at all stages, including project preparation, implementation, and evaluation. Data Source: Supervision consultant's annual reports, and project completion report from KazAvtoZhol Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2024 Target value: Y Actual value: N

Output: Institutional capacity of KazAvtoZhol strengthened Indicator: Equipment to strengthen KazAvtoZhol branch offices delivered Achievement: Y Progress/Status: During the mid-term review, KAZH requested the mission to replace the planned activity with a training program on road maintenance and FIDIC contracts, noting that the procurement of office equipment for both branch and head offices is being financed from its own funds. Since the output indicator 2a already includes the necessary training activities, it was agreed to (i) retain the output 2c as originally formulated for further monitoring in its original form and (ii) monitor KAZH's provision of KAZH supplying the office and road maintenance equipment. In 2023, KAZH procured 120 units of office equipment and furniture valued at $120,000 (KZT 58 million) and indicated that equipment renewal follows a five-year cycle. In 2024, KAZH entered into financial leasing agreements with the Kazakhstan Industrial Development Fund (KIDF) to acquire 500 units of road maintenance equipment for maintaining toll roads. The PMU reported that no equipment was purchased in 2025 under KIDF or IFI-financed projects, as the current equipment is adequate for KAZH's operational needs. The PMU has committed to updating the mission in due course on any new plan to renovate the current equipment fleet (plans for renewing both the office and maintenance equipment) until the approval of the Project Completion Report (PCR) for ADB's approval. Data Source: Supervision consultant's annual reports, and project completion report from KazAvtoZhol Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Baseline year: 2019 Baseline value: N Target year: 2024 Target value: Y Actual value: Y

Output: Institutional capacity of KazAvtoZhol strengthened Indicator: Implementation plan to improve KazAvtoZhol's financial position developed Achievement: Y Progress/Status: KAZH's financial sustainability relies on the (i) the Republican Budget funds earmarked for Trust Management Agreements signed with the Ministry of Finance (MOF), Ministry of Transport, and KAZH under which expenses related to road construction and maintenance, toll collection are reimbursed as well as repayment of IFI loans; and (ii) tolls collected from 3,200 km of republican roads, with the plan to increase the network of toll roads to 7,000 km by the end of 2025. The tolls are used to pay the cost of routine repair and maintenance of toll roads on self-financed basis and make payments for the leasing of maintenance equipment. KAZH will provide the status of the implementation plan.
